mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in the federal funds rate above 4.5% for two consecutive months signals a restrictive monetary policy stance, raising discount rates and reducing present value of corporate cash flows, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered episodes, or the negative rank IC falls below 0.10.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) exceeding 2% coincident with a housing starts (HOUST) contraction of more than 10% month-over-month predicts weakening consumer and construction demand, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 40% of triggered episodes, or the mechanism fails when unemployment is simultaneously falling.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly increase in industrial production (INDPRO) of at least 0.5% for three consecutive months signals strengthening manufacturing activity, which boosts corporate earnings expectations and drives positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO > previous month +0.5% for 3 consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not statistically different from zero in more than 60% of triggered months.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly unemployment rate (UNRATE) falling below 3.5% for two consecutive months, accompanied by a concurrent rise in average hourly earnings (PAYEMS growth > 0.3% month-over-month), signals a tight labor market with upward wage pressure, which erodes corporate margins and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE < 3.5% for 2 consecutive months AND PAYEMS MoM growth > 0.3%
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered episodes, or the mechanism fails when inflation exceeds 5%.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp decline in the Consumer Price Index for All Urban Consumers (CPIAUCSL) of more than 0.6% month-over-month signals a deflationary shock, prompting the Federal Reserve to cut rates, which supports equity valuations and produces positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly above zero in more than 70% of triggered deflation episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A sequential rise in retail sales (RSAFS) of at least 1% month-over-month for four consecutive months, with concurrent strength in housing starts (HOUST), signals robust consumer demand, which lifts corporate earnings and drives positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: RSAFS MoM > 1% for 4 consecutive months AND HOUST MoM > 0%
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not statistically different from zero in more than 50% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) above 6.5% for three consecutive months signals a deepening labor market weakness, which depresses consumer spending and corporate profits, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 40% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly contraction in industrial production (INDPRO) of more than 0.4% for five consecutive months signals a broad-based manufacturing slowdown, which reduces earnings expectations and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly below zero in more than 60% of triggered episodes.
